title: Randomized Laplacian estimate off notable coordinates
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces whose coordinate atom weights are strictly positive and sum to one, and let $\Omega=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}\Omega_j$ be its outcome space. For $f\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $x\in\Omega$, a coordinate $i$, and $\tau>0$, suppose $i$ is not notable at $x$, meaning $\tau>\sum_{S\ni i}f_S(x)^2$, where $f_S$ is the $S$-component of $f$. Set $g=T_{2/5}L_i f$ and $h(r)=\sum_S\chi_S(r)g_S(x)$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, using the product spectral noise and components and the Walsh characters on the Boolean cube. Then, with cube power means taken under the uniform measure, $\|T_{1/\sqrt3}h\|_2^2\le\tau^{1/3}\|h\|_{4/3}^{4/3}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with positive coordinate weights summing to one
$i$ is not in the set of coordinates whose local spectral influence at $x$ is at least $\tau$
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $x\in\Omega$, a coordinate $i$, and $\tau>0$. If $\sum_{S\ni i}f_S(x)^2<\tau$, put $g=T_{2/5}L_if$ and $h(r)=\sum_S\chi_S(r)g_S(x)$; then on the uniform sign cube $\|T_{1/\sqrt3}h\|_2^2\le\tau^{1/3}\|h\|_{4/3}^{4/3}$.
